name: earnings_news_jar
themes: Company KPI and alt-data backtest repos for ABNB or OTAs: anyone who already assembled Airbnb quarterly KPI datasets, consensus, or alt-data panels
one_line: Replication code for Grégoire & Martineau (JAR), 'How Is Earnings News Transmitted to Stock Prices?'; MIT, 11 stars, last push 2021-07-12, 44 KB total — root holds only IBES/, RavenPack/, TRTH/, Sample_Stocks/ code folders and a README; every input (RavenPack news, IBES surprises, ~12 TB Refinitiv Tick History, Nasdaq ITCH) is licensed and none is committed.
abnb_use: Gap #17 as a citable methodology for how earnings news gets impounded intraday — relevant only if we ever wanted to characterise the 5 Nov print's price path; no KPI, travel or consensus data.
sample_plan: No pull. There is no data/ directory (confirmed via `gh api repos/vgreg/earnings_news_jar/contents`) and the only CSV is a sample stock-identifier list; the pipeline needs RavenPack + IBES + TRTH/ITCH, all paid and none redistributable.
what_it_holds: Code (59% Python, 41% Jupyter Notebook) accompanying the paper "How Is Earnings News Transmitted to Stock Prices?" — an academic replication package studying earnings-announcement information transmission, not company-specific but a methods reference for event-study construction around earnings prints.
review_reasoning: Root listing confirms code-only folders with no committed data, and the README names RavenPack, IBES, TRTH and ITCH as inputs — every one paid or licensed, so the repo can never yield free data. The MIT code is a legitimate published methodology reference for intraday earnings-news transmission, which is why it is catalogued rather than discarded. Dormant since Jul 2021.
